summary: ORION is an on-board health monitoring and forecasting tool for long-duration crews. It reads a passive wrist watch the astronaut never has to touch, adds live NASA space-weather data, and forecasts each crew member's health seven days ahead. It explains every score in plain language and recommends a first action. It runs fully offline, because from Mars a question to Earth can take 40 minutes to answer.
details:
THE PROBLEM
On Moon and Mars missions, astronauts face radiation, isolation, altered gravity, and closed environments for months, while communication with Earth can be delayed by up to 40 minutes one way. Immune changes, bone loss, cardiovascular events, eye and brain changes (SANS), fatigue, and behavioral health problems can build slowly. The crew is increasingly responsible for spotting them in themselves, and most existing tools only show today's numbers and need constant manual input.

WHAT ORION DOES
ORION turns raw health signals into a clear, forward-looking answer to three questions: How am I now? What will change this week? What should I do?

- Passive data: a wrist actigraph provides sleep, resting heart rate, heart-rate variability, and skin temperature, so the crew has nothing to type.
- Live space weather: ORION pulls solar flare, coronal mass ejection, geomagnetic storm, and solar energetic particle events from NASA DONKI and uses them to adjust the radiation-related risk scores.
- 7-day forecast: for every crew member, ORION shows 14 days of measured data and a 7-day forecast across seven areas: fatigue and performance, immune response, radiation dose, heart and circulation, bone and muscle, eye and brain (SANS), and spacewalk readiness.
- Plain-language status: each area has a 0-100 risk index with color AND icon AND label (Normal, Watch, Elevated, Critical), so status is never conveyed by color alone.
- Explainable by design: every score shows what drove it, such as sleep loss, heart-rate drift, or a solar particle event. There is no black box.
- First order: when risk rises, ORION shows the single most important action first, such as moving a spacewalk by 24 hours or swapping the crew member, followed by further countermeasures.
- What-if controls: users can switch between Low Earth orbit, Lunar orbit, and Mars transit, change the mission day, and simulate events such as a solar particle event to see the forecast change instantly.
- Crew and flight-surgeon view: one crew selector, with a plain-language daily summary that can be shared with the flight surgeon on Earth when the link is available.

HOW IT WORKS
ORION builds a personal baseline for each astronaut from their own recent data. It measures deviation from that baseline, extrapolates the trend, and applies space-weather modifiers. The forecast engine runs entirely on the client, is deterministic, and is unit-tested, so results are reproducible and can be audited. All data stays on the device. The app is a PWA, so it works with no network and falls back to cached NASA data with a visible timestamp.

NASA DATA AND RESOURCES USED
- NASA Open APIs: DONKI space weather data (FLR, CME, GST, SEP) for live radiation-related context.
- NASA Human Research Program: the five hazards of human spaceflight (radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile closed environments). Every indicator in ORION is mapped to a hazard and a body system.
- Spaceflight Standard Measures and Artemis II Standard Measures: used as scientific grounding for which physiological systems and indicators matter on long missions.
- Canadian Space Agency material on how spaceflight affects bones, heart, brain, and balance.

WHY IT MATTERS
Earlier warning gives the crew time to change workouts, sleep schedules, nutrition, EVA plans, or shelter before a problem becomes critical. The same idea can help on Earth too: passive monitoring and personal baselines are useful for older adults, remote workers, and people in isolated environments.

DESIGN
ORION uses a minimal, Apple-inspired interface: a dark canvas, restrained accent color, glass surfaces, and a macOS-style animated dock for navigation. It is designed for tired people in stressful situations, with large type, plain language, and keyboard and touch support.

TECHNOLOGY
React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, [charting library], PWA/service worker, IndexedDB for local storage, Vitest for the forecast engine tests.
